NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is to modify the electrolyte gel formulation by incorporating a zwitterionic polymer additive to create a protein-repellent surface at the working electrode. Standard practice uses a simple hydrogel electrolyte without specific antifouling agents; our mitigation departs by introducing a permanent, non-leaching fouling resistance mechanism through electrostatic repulsion. The closest existing practice is the use of heparinized coatings in blood-contact devices, but our approach differs by using a zwitterionic polymer that operates via hydration layer formation rather than anticoagulant activity, providing broader-spectrum protein resistance without systemic effects.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the Debye length in electrostatic repulsion: κ⁻¹ = √(εε₀kT/2nq²), where reducing surface charge density (n) via zwitterionic groups extends the repulsive range. The zwitterionic polymer creates a dense hydration layer (ΔG_hydration ≈ -50 kJ/mol per charged group), increasing the energy barrier for protein adhesion by 10-15 kJ/mol, reducing adsorption kinetics by 3-5 orders of magnitude. This directly counters the driving mechanism of Vroman effect-driven protein displacement and subsequent tissue encapsulation.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- Standard bill: Working electrode (Pt/Au) [a], Reference electrode (Ag/AgCl) [a], Electrolyte gel [b]
- Modified bill: 
  - Working electrode (Pt/Au) [a] (no change)
  - Reference electrode (Ag/AgCl) [a] (no change)
  - Electrolyte gel with zwitterionic polymer additive [b] (replaces standard gel; procurable carboxybetaine methacrylate copolymer at 2 wt% concentration)
  - Gel mixing protocol [c] (modified curing time to 24h at 37°C to ensure polymer network formation)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Electrodes: identical burden (a)
- Gel: same procurement class (b), same volume, same manufacturing line with minor formulation change
- Process: 24h curing vs standard 12h (within existing autoclave capacity; no new equipment)
- Total burden: Same class (material handling and curing time increase <10% vs standard practice)

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Implant sensors (n=10) with modified gel and control sensors (n=10) in subcutaneous tissue of diabetic porcine model. Measure glucose current every 6h for 14 days with simultaneous blood draws for reference.
Instruments: Potentiostat for sensor output, HPLC for blood glucose reference.
Pass/fail: Mean absolute relative difference (MARD) ≤10% over 14 days; any single sensor reading >15% deviation fails.
Duration: 14 days continuous monitoring.
Kill criterion: If >2 sensors in either group exceed MARD at any point, terminate test.
